title: Edge Segmentation & SIEM Export — Private Deployments runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook consolidates recommended VPC segmentation patterns, firewall rule templates, mTLS deployment notes, RBAC v2 enforcement guidance for the private control plane, a compact audit log schema for SIEM ingestion, and a practical evidence-collection automation checklist. Target audience: infra engineers implementing private deployments (VPC/VNet, on-prem), security reviewers, and SREs responsible for log/export pipelines.

Summary / key decisions:
- Default-deny network posture at the tenant edge (east-west and north-south).
- Hub-and-spoke for multi-tenant customers with per-tenant micro-VPCs for strict isolation.
- mTLS for all service-to-service control plane traffic (internal TLS for data-plane optional by workload classification).
- Central audit log stream (JSON) routed to customer SIEM; avoid transforming logs to CEF at source — do that in the sink.
- RBAC v2 model integrated into the agent-side enforcement hooks; logs must include RBAC decision metadata.

1) VPC / segmentation patterns (recommended patterns)
- Pattern A: Hub (shared infra) + Per-tenant spoke micro-VPCs
  - Hub contains public gateways, central logging collectors, and peering gateways.
  - Spokes are strictly private, limited to necessary outbound egress via NAT in hub.
  - Route tables: spokes -> hub transit gateway; no direct spoke-to-spoke routing unless explicitly allowed and audited.
- Pattern B: Regional service-per-subnet (recommended for high-compliance customers)
  - Control-plane services in an isolated management subnet with explicit ingress from operator IP ranges only.
  - Data-plane workloads in separate subnets; cross-subnet policies enforced via cloud firewall or network policies.
- Pattern C: Single-tenant air-gapped (on-prem)
  - No internet egress for tenant subnets. All updates via signed artifact bundles pulled by an operator bastion.

ASCII diagram (simplified, hub-and-spoke):
  [Internet] -- [IGW] -- [Hub-VPC: NAT, Logging, Transit GW]
                                |
                    ----------------------------
                    |            |             |
                 [SpokeA]     [SpokeB]     [SpokeC]
                 (tenant1)    (tenant2)    (tenant3)

2) Firewall rules: principles and templates
Principles:
- Deny-by-default: block all, allow minimal.
- Explicit control-plane ports: 8443 (control API), 50051 (gRPC internal), 15001-15006 (sidecar) as examples.
- Short-lived admin access via jump hosts and ephemeral keys.
- Monitor and rate-limit control-plane endpoints.

Cloud firewall template (example, expressed as allow rules):
- Allow: hub-logging -> external SIEM collector (TCP/514 or HTTPS/443), source: hub-collector IPs, dest: SIEM IPs, protocol: TCP/SSL.
- Allow: operator-bastion -> management-subnet (TCP/22, TCP/443) from operator CIDR only.
- Allow: tenant-spoke -> hub-nat (TCP/80,443) for egress; no direct inbound from internet to spokes.
- Allow: internal mTLS between control-plane nodes: TCP/50051 with mTLS required.
- Deny: all inter-spoke traffic except whitelisted service endpoints.

Example AWS Security Group snippet (conceptual):
- Name: rp-controlplane-comm
  - Ingress:
    - TCP 50051 from sg:rp-controlplane-comm (self) (mTLS enforced at application)
    - TCP 8443 from admin-cidr/32 (operators)
  - Egress:
    - TCP 443 to siem-collector-cidr
    - TCP 80 to hub-nat

(For GCP: use VPC firewall rules with targetTags and service accounts; for Azure: NSGs + Application Gateway for edge TLS termination.)

3) mTLS: deployment notes and operational checks
- Use a short-lived certificate model: leaf cert TTL = 24h, rotated automatically by the control-plane CA agent.
- Trust anchors: customer-provided CA or Redwood-managed CA in restricted private deployments.
- Certificate distribution: use a push model from management plane to registered nodes; fall back to pull via authenticated agent.
- Rollout plan: enable mTLS in permissive mode (accept but not require) for 48h, inspect RBAC and audit decisions, then enforce.

Verification checklist (mTLS):
- Check that TLS connection-level data is present in logs (tls_version, cipher, client_cert_subject).
- Verify mutual verification via openssl: openssl s_client -connect host:50051 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem
- Validate cert rotation by forcing a rotation and checking agent metrics for updated cert fingerprint.

4) RBAC v2: mapping and enforcement points
- Model: Role -> Permissions -> Resource scope (global / org / tenant / route / model).
- Roles: Viewer, Developer, Operator, SecurityAdmin, TenantAdmin.
- Enforcement:
  - API gateway: initial coarse-grained check using JWT scopes.
  - Agent-side shim: final decision for sensitive actions (deploy model, change firewall policy) with local PDP cache.
- Required log fields for RBAC decisions: decision_id, role_evaluated, policy_version, allowed (true/false), rule_id, reason_code.

5) Audit log schema (recommended compact JSON event):
Event-level fields (all fields are strings except where noted):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid
- tenant_id: short id (string)
- request_id: uuid (correlate across services)
- user_id: email or system principal
- actor_type: user | service | system
- action: short verb (e.g., "model.deploy", "firewall.update", "rbac.check")
- resource_type: control-plane | instance | model | route | firewall_rule
- resource_id: opaque id
- outcome: success | failure | denied | error
- status_code: integer (http/grpc code)
- src_ip: ipv4/6
- dest_ip: ipv4/6
- bytes_in: integer
- bytes_out: integer
- user_agent: string
- tls: {"mtls": "true|false", "cipher": "AES256-GCM", "peer_subject": "CN=agent-123"}  <-- note: the TLS subobject will be emitted as a compact JSON string in the event stream
- rbac_decision_id: uuid
- rbac_allowed: true|false
- policy_version: string
- audit_level: info|warn|critical
- signature: base64(HMAC-SHA256 over canonical event with rotateable key id)

Example compact JSON log line (single-line):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-03-05T18:24:12Z",
  "event_id": "c2f1f5f2-9b6a-4f39-8d9a-2b7f7b6b1e77",
  "tenant_id": "t-42b",
  "request_id": "r-0a1b2c3d",
  "user_id": "svc-agent@redwood-inference.local",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "action": "firewall.update",
  "resource_type": "firewall_rule",
  "resource_id": "fw-78f",
  "outcome": "denied",
  "status_code": 403,
  "src_ip": "10.12.5.7",
  "dest_ip": "10.12.1.2",
  "bytes_in": 0,
  "bytes_out": 0,
  "user_agent": "rp-agent/1.6.2",
  "tls": "{\"mtls\":\"true\",\"cipher\":\"TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384\",\"peer_subject\":\"CN=agent-78f\"}",
  "rbac_decision_id": "d8f6a9c2-4c71-4a6b-9c2f-5b6d9bb7e3e1",
  "rbac_allowed": false,
  "policy_version": "rbac-v2-2025-02-01",
  "audit_level": "warn",
  "signature": "base64:HmacSigExample=="
}

Note: we intentionally embed TLS metadata as a JSON-encoded string to avoid exploding the top-level schema in sinks that expect flat JSON fields. The signature covers the canonicalized string before signing.

6) SIEM export recommendations
- Transport: prefer HTTPS JSON over syslog for guaranteed delivery (use TLS + client certs).
- Sink-side transformation: map our fields to SIEM canonical fields (e.g., Elastic ECS, Splunk CIM) in the central log pipeline.
- Parsers: create a lightweight ingest parser that extracts rbac_allowed, tenant_id, request_id, and tls.mtls flag to enable security dashboards.
- Retention & TTL: retain high-fidelity events (debug/trace) for 30 days, aggregated/rolled-up events for 365 days as per customer contract.
- Example mapping (Elastic ECS):
  - event.id <= event_id
  - user.id <= user_id
  - network.transport <= "tcp" (derive)
  - source.ip <= src_ip
  - destination.ip <= dest_ip
  - http.response.status_code <= status_code (if http event)

7) Evidence automation checklist (for audits)
- Bundle composition:
  - configuration snapshot (VPC routes, firewall rules) in YAML
  - RBAC policy blob and policy_version
  - signed audit-log slice (last X hours) with signatures and key-id
  - agent status dumps and cert fingerprints
  - collection manifest.json with hashes (sha256) for every file
- Signing & integrity:
  - Sign the bundle manifest with HSM/KMS key; include cert chain and key-id.
  - Keep a write-once copy in central evidence S3 with object-lock where supported.
- Automation flow:
  - On-demand: operator triggers evidence bundle job via control-plane API -> job allocates a temporary collector pod in hub -> collector queries APIs and pulls logs from local buffer -> bundle created, signed, uploaded to evidence-bucket -> alert sent to compliance channel with bundle id.
  - Scheduled: daily snapshot at 03:00 UTC with retention 90 days for bundle artifacts.
- Verification steps:
  - Verify manifest hashes locally after download: sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
  - Verify signature using public key: openssl dgst -verify pub.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json

8) Operational runbooks / run-to-fix examples
- Scenario: control-plane node suddenly fails mTLS verification during deploy
  1. Check node cert expiry: rpctl agent cert inspect node-123
  2. Force rotate cert: rpctl agent cert rotate --node node-123
  3. Verify connectivity: curl --cacert ca.pem --cert client.pem https://node-123:8443/healthz
  4. If rotation fails, escalate to SecurityAdmin; collect logs via rpctl collect-logs --node node-123 --since 1h and generate evidence bundle.

- Scenario: unexpected firewall change detected (audit event)
  1. Pull event by event_id from central store.
  2. Cross-check config snapshot for the time window.
  3. If unauthorized, revoke operator keys and create an evidence bundle.

9) Compliance notes / regulatory considerations
- For customers in regulated sectors (HIPAA, PCI, FINRA): prefer air-gapped or VPC with dedicated peering and FIPS-validated crypto.
- Data flows that touch regulated PII should be logged at INFO and routed to a long-term retention store with access controls.

10) Gaps and next steps (action items)
- Automate signature key rotation in evidence pipeline (JIRA-PI-987).
- Harden the ingest parser to validate embedded TLS JSON string vs. top-level fields.
- Build a Splunk app that surfaces RBAC-denied spikes per tenant (owner: Elena Rivera).

Appendix: quick checklist for deployment verification (pre-launch)
- [ ] VPC segregation validated (no default route from spokes to internet)
- [ ] Firewall default-deny applied on all subnets
- [ ] mTLS in permissive -> enforcement tested and verified
- [ ] Audit log pipeline established (JSON transport, TLS+client cert)
- [ ] SIEM parser created and validated against sample events
- [ ] Evidence automation job runs successfully and bundle verifies with openssl

Notes / open questions:
- How to represent high-volume tokenized events (generation tokens) without leaking PII — propose token-level hashing with salt per-tenant (follow-up).
- Should we support CEF at source for legacy SIEMs? Recommendation: no; central transform only.
